concept.reason: Primary true adult skull and reconstruction provide sufficient crest architecture, no extra concept image.

scope: Complete lightly built tyrannosauroid with thin perforated median cranial crest, long three-fingered arms and full trunk, hindlimbs and tail.

scientific_limits.en: Adult IVPP V14531 skull and partial skeleton anchor anatomy and about3m length; Fig1 skeleton photograph is juvenile V14532, not the adult. Supplementary true adult skull photos and Fig2 reconstruction show preserved crest fenestrae and a missing anterior crest region. Bone perforation is fossil evidence, but skin spanning openings, external covering and colour unknown. Do not assert exposed living holes as established fact. Missing crest portion, soft tissues and pose reconstructed.
scientific_limits.zh: 成年V14531头骨及部分骨架为主锚，原文约3米；图1骨架照片为幼体V14532，不能冒称成年。补充成年真颅照片与图2复原明确冠部骨窗及缺失前冠。骨性穿孔为化石事实，但皮肤是否跨窗、外覆和颜色未知，不能称活体露天孔洞已证实。缺失冠、软组织和姿态均复原。

scale.basis: Xu etal2006 about3m holotype body length, approximate not exact complete living measurement.

diagnostic_targets: One thin tall sagittal blade crest over most skull roof, narrow in frontal/top views, not paired Dilophosaurus crests.
Preserve bone architecture of large posterior pneumatic fenestra plus two smaller anterior/ventral windows and four supporting lateral laminae; no solid featureless helmet.
Render crest windows open as an explicitly labelled artistic choice exposing known bony framework, not a claim that living skin necessarily had holes; retain the original perforated gate.
Light body with long forelimbs, three clawed digits and inward palms; forelimb a little under60percent hindlimb per paper.
Long neck, slender body and balancing tail, not scaled-down bulky adult Tyrannosaurus.
specimen_basis: Actually viewed primary Fig1 juvenile skeleton, Fig2 adult cranial/digit reconstruction, supplementary Fig1 true adult skull lateral/dorsal/ventrolateral views.
acceptance_checks: Original gate thin perforated midline crest on lightly built tyrannosauroid retained; neither opaque bulky crown nor double crests.
Compare standard side view directly to adult Fig2 and supplementary skull photo: posterior window and smaller support structures positioned faithfully, restored anterior area disclosed.
Front/top show single thin median blade with lateral supports; not Guanlong distinction by name, scale or pose alone.
Whole body retains long three-fingered forelimbs; juvenile skeleton does not silently set adult proportions.
Scientific limits must separate fossil bone fenestrae from inferred living skin treatment. Four standard views, no original named same-pose extra-render requirement.
